Mapping verification is PARTIAL: the deposit's own CE/AE totals reproduce exactly for 523/523 respondents under Reniers' subscale membership with items 1,2,17,29 reversed, and polarity pins QCAE1 (only reverse OS item, r = -0.398) and QCAE11 (only forward PER item, r = -0.521), but order WITHIN a subscale rests on the item numbering, not on the data. PARTIAL COVERAGE: 1 of 3 item stems recovered. Powell et al. 2018 (PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0194569) used 'an adapted version of the English-version of the German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP) Trust scale' with the object changed to 'staff/students at the host university', and prints exactly one adapted item as an example: 'In general, you can trust staff/students at the host university'. That is shipped on Trust1. No wording is published anywhere for Trust2 or Trust3, so those ship blank item_text rather than a guess. Checked and found no item wording in: the article body, S1 Text (game instructions), S2 Text (dataset variable definitions -- lists Trust# only as 'Response to trust question #', Ordinal 1-4), S3 Text, S1 Dataset (S005 CSV, bare column headers Trust1/Trust2/Trust3/rTrust3/TrustScore). Data Availability names no external repository, and a Europe PMC full-text search for 'staff/students at the host university' returns this paper alone. CANONICAL WORDING DELIBERATELY NOT SUBSTITUTED: the parent SOEP-Trust index (Naef & Schupp 2009, IZA DP 4087, p.6) is 'In general, you can trust people.' / "Nowadays, you can't rely on anybody." / "It's better to be cautious before trusting strangers." -- two of three negatively worded. This administration has exactly ONE reverse-keyed item: the S1 file carries rTrust3 and no rTrust1/rTrust2, TrustScore = Trust1 + Trust2 + (5 - Trust3) reproduces for 523/523 respondents, and in the live table r(Trust1,Trust2)=+0.68 while r(*,Trust3)=-0.40/-0.45. So the adaptation demonstrably departs from the canonical wording for at least one item, and dropping canonical text onto Trust2/Trust3 would fabricate both the words and the mapping. OPTION ANCHORS: the paper states only the endpoints (1 = disagree strongly, 4 = agree strongly); resp 2 and 3 ('disagree somewhat', 'agree somewhat') are the parent instrument's own middle anchors from Naef & Schupp p.6, whose four-point scale the paper's endpoints match verbatim. INSTRUCTIONS left blank -- the paper describes the response format but reproduces no instruction text. RIGHTS: no reserved right locatable for SOEP-Trust; it is published in full in an open DIW/IZA discussion paper with no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause, and no entry in instrument_rights_register.csv. Item wording is transcribed as printed, without a trailing period, since the paper prints it that way inside its parenthetical example. AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (audit_batch.R: '66.7% of rows have blank item_text'): expected and correct, NOT an itemtext defect and not a response-data defect either. The table has 3 items and the source publishes only 1 of the 3 adapted stems, so Trust2 and Trust3 ship blank item_text by design -- 8 of 12 rows (66.7%) blank is exactly 2 items x 4 response levels. Padding them with canonical SOEP-Trust wording was rejected deliberately: the parent SOEP index has two negatively worded items of three and this administration has exactly one (orchestrator re-check of the source S1 Dataset, n=523, confirms only rTrust3 exists, no rTrust1/rTrust2; TrustScore = Trust1 + Trust2 + (5 - Trust3) reproduces the file's own TrustScore 523/523; r(Trust1,Trust2)=+0.677 while r(Trust1,Trust3)=-0.399 and r(Trust2,Trust3)=-0.445), so at least one item was reworded and canonical text would have fabricated both the wording and its placement. The WARN clears only if the authors publish the two remaining adapted stems.

Clean pass, but with four caveats a reader needs. (1) TWO ADMINISTERED LANGUAGES IN ONE FIELD. The .sav's own variable @41Idioma ('Idioma en el que rellena la encuesta') records that 93 of the 101 respondents completed the Arabic form and 8 the French form. The schema has one item_text field, so both administered wordings ship in it, marked '[Arabic version] ... [French version] ...', following the precedent set by PMT_Trzcinska_2023_PMT in batch_141; language is recorded as 'Arabic; French'. Neither form is invented -- both are transcribed from Table S1 of the study team's own companion validation paper (Bas-Sarmiento, Poza-Mendez, Fernandez-Gutierrez, Gonzalez-Caballero & Falcon, 2020, Int. J. Environ. Res. Public Health 17(21):8181, doi:10.3390/ijerph17218181, CC BY 4.0), which is the paper the source article cites for 'The French and Arabic version used has been adapted and validated in an immigrant population'. (2) THE ARABIC WAS REPAIRED, MECHANICALLY AND REVERSIBLY. Table S1 is a PDF; pdftotext emits every lam-alef ligature with its two characters in the wrong order (LAM+ALEF comes out as ALEF+LAM), so raw extraction reads e.g. 'AAlAjAt' for 'ilajat'. The 16 strings shipped were repaired by hand and then round-trip checked: re-applying the corruption rule (swap LAM followed by any alef variant) to each shipped string reproduces the pdftotext byte stream exactly for all 16 items (items 12 and 16 verified fragment-wise, because bidi reorders their punctuation-delimited segments across a line break). So the only change made to the extracted Arabic is ligature ordering; nothing was re-worded. The transcription was also read against a 200-dpi render of the page. (3) ITEM 8'S ARABIC IS DEFECTIVE IN THE SOURCE ITSELF. It reads 'or stress / the way of dealing with mental illness problems such as depression...' -- the phrase 'or stress' sits at the front instead of the end, and 'bi-tariqa' is joined to the preceding word. The rendered page shows the same thing, so this is the authors' own typesetting defect and it is transcribed as printed rather than silently repaired. Its French twin is intact and its identity is not in doubt. (4) THE RESPONSE ANCHORS ARE SPANISH, NOT ARABIC OR FRENCH. Respondents answered on a 4-point scale (very difficult ... very easy); the IRW table stores the study's dichotomisation, and the only published tie between 0/1 and any words is the .sav's own value labels, 'DIFICIL/MUY DIFICIL' = 0 and 'MUY FACIL/FACIL' = 1, which are Spanish. Those are shipped verbatim rather than a back-translation into the administered languages, which the deposit and both papers never print. Same shape as aguirre_camacho_2021_champion. INSTRUCTIONS are blank: neither Table S1 nor either paper prints the instrument's stem sentence, and it was not invented. SUBSAMPLE: the deposit's .sav has 101 respondents while the Nursing Open paper reports 278 and the validation paper 205; the IRW table is the deposited subset. Not an itemtext issue, but it means the papers' published statistics will not reproduce from this table. ENGLISH: the _translated columns were written by IRW from the administered Arabic and French, not by the authors -- neither paper prints an English rendering of this adaptation, and the adaptation diverges from the canonical HLS-EU-Q16 English in places (item 10 names a breast exam, blood sugar and blood pressure; item 2's Arabic adds '(e.g. a doctor, a pharmacist or a psychologist)' where the French does not). Hence translation_source=machine_translation, which owes an issues-page entry. RIGHTS: no row in instrument_rights_register.csv matches the HLS-EU-Q16 or any health-literacy instrument. The wording shipped is not the HLS-EU consortium's original English but this team's own Arabic/French adaptation, printed as Table S1 of a CC BY 4.0 IJERPH article whose own caption reads 'Source: Own elaboration'. The validation paper's acknowledgements thank the HLS-EU project 'for providing the items of the short version' -- a courtesy acknowledgement, not a reserved right. No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was located for the HLS-EU-Q16: m-pohl.net returned nothing of the kind on its front page and m-pohl.net/HLS19_Instruments returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-10, and the web-search tool was unavailable that day, so no clause is quoted here. Under 'silence is permission' it ships, but that is an absence of evidence rather than a checked all-clear -- a later pass with working search should register a verdict for the HLS-EU-Q family.
